grand_strategy.reading: Australia is the ally that pays for a guarantor that may not come, and the regional order it is building is the insurance on that premium. Everything since 2023 reads as one move: lock the United States in with submarines, minerals and a statute that survived a Pentagon review (AUKUS, endorsed December 2025; the framework signed on 20 Oct 2025), while turning every neighbour into a treaty partner that screens out China - Papua New Guinea as a mutual-defence ally (2025), Fiji as the fourth ally (6 Jul 2026), vetoes in Nauru and Tuvalu, no foreign bases in Vanuatu, a treaty bid for the Solomon Islands, a security treaty with Indonesia. The Albanese government has a free hand to do this: re-elected in May 2025 with 94 of 150 seats, it faces an opposition that attacks it for weakness on China rather than for the direction. The Luttwakian pattern is in the gap between the two halves. The guarantee is bought at the price of entanglement (an Australian crew aboard the submarine that sank the Dena) and is still conditional (3.5% asked, a Taiwan pre-commitment reportedly asked for, a 10% tariff in April 2025, a five-month review of the flagship programme), while the insurance is built by buying sovereignty from the very islands it is meant to protect, who answer by bargaining. Two signals that are not rows: Albanese's first reply to the Tasman drills was to stress that China had complied with international law, and the New Delhi Quad meeting of May 2026 spoke of tolls in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, which points to the Iran war rather than the Taiwan Strait. The question for 2027 is whether the ring of treaties and the submarine timetable hold long enough to outlast the guarantor's moods; the first stress test is the Solomon Islands treaty, which a Solomon Islands minister floated for the end of 2026.

stances.note: ANZUS (1951), AUKUS and the AUSMIN process make this the structural alliance, and in 2025-26 the formal ties grew: the Pentagon's review ended in December 2025 with an endorsement of the sale of at least three Virginia-class boats from 2032 and 'critical deadlines' for all three capitals; on 20 Oct 2025 Trump told Albanese the programme was going 'full steam ahead' and the two signed a critical-minerals framework (at least US$1bn of co-financing in six months, a US$8.5bn pipeline). The friction is recorded and real - the 10% 'Liberation Day' tariff (Albanese: 'not the act of a friend'), Hegseth's request at Shangri-La 2025 for 3.5% of GDP, Elbridge Colby's reported push for a pre-commitment on Taiwan, Trump's public rebuke of Ambassador Rudd - but each time Canberra paid or deferred rather than distanced itself (the April 2026 defence strategy sets 3% by 2033 under NATO accounting, not 3.5%), and ADF personnel were aboard a US submarine in the 2026 Iran war. Held at ally, not reluctant ally: no source reads Canberra's side as grudging, and the Wong line on the June 2025 US strikes on Iran was support. Stable because the treaty layer thickened while the trust question (will the guarantor come?) did not move. Bond - kin: Anglosphere, Five Eyes, war memory. The USA card is being written in parallel; reconcile the pair after it lands.
